name: Skeletal
function: Show the skeletal framework that supports the trunk and links it to the limbs.
verdict: Compare the right knee in its source pose and at 20° more flexion. The femur stays fixed, the tibia and fibula rotate together, and arrows indicate qualitative load directions.
gaps: The tibial plateau clears the femur in both sampled poses. The hinge omits rolling, gliding and soft-tissue loading. The skeleton’s 271 representation meshes include bone, cartilage/disc and dental categories.
baselineCombined: The atlas preserves its native BodyParts3D positions. The model shows gross support and spatial relationships.
Separate Z-Anatomy joint study. Bone and soft-tissue structures already share the supplied scene.

name: Muscular
function: Trace calf muscle force through the Achilles tendon to the heel.
verdict: Follow gastrocnemius and soleus through the Achilles tendon to the calcaneus in neutral and 15° plantarflexion.
gaps: Five sampled poses preserve the distal 0.085 mm attachment witness. The native talus and fibula overlap in neutral. Whole-body insertions, clinical biomechanics and rig coverage remain open.
baselineCombined: This reviewer-inspected static supplement shows the tendon and nearby bone landmarks. Use the whole-body atlas as an orientation plate.

name: Respiratory
function: Show how the diaphragm and lungs change together during one breath.
verdict: Follow air from the nasal cavity through the pharynx and larynx, along the trachea to a left lobar branch and an enlarged alveolar cluster. Open the gas-exchange stage from the terminal focus.
gaps: Fourteen neighbour checks and four cup-wall ray tests passed. The lobar and smaller airways are schematic and compressed. The local Chrome lesson was exercised at rest and during inspiration, through all four airway views and into the separate exchange diagram.
baselineCombined: Still of paired breathing GLBs and the authored diaphragm in their delivered frame. Motion was not re-evaluated here.
Shared frame · lungs and lobar airway
Workshop scene with the authored lobar hierarchy. The opaque lung exterior naturally hides distal branches, which are isolated below.

name: Urinary
function: Trace urine from both kidneys down the ureters to the bladder and outlet.
verdict: Inspect each renal pelvis, ureter, trigone entry and the shared outlet in Workshop coordinates. The enlarged renal corpuscle separates the blood and filtrate paths.
gaps: Ten junctions were checked on both participating surfaces. Teaching sections, added ureters, flow arrows and the filtration inset are schematic. Seams remain visible between some adjoining tubes.
baselineCombined: Kidney exteriors and the authored bladder system from the Workshop. The illustrated ureter course and outlet support gross route teaching.

name: Cardiovascular
function: Follow blood through the pulmonary and systemic loops.
verdict: Trace one directional loop through both sides of the heart, its four valves and the schematic pulmonary and systemic vascular beds.
gaps: All twenty endpoints were checked at ten transitions. The source chamber and leaflet shapes occupy exploded teaching positions. Vessel bridges and beds are authored.
baselineCombined: Workshop heart shell with aorta and pulmonary venous surface. Regions outside this selection and an actual closed loop remain uncovered.

name: Digestive
function: Trace food from intake through the gut, with accessory organs placed relative to their delivery points.
verdict: Follow the opened, uncoiled food route from mouth to outlet, alongside the source exteriors. Isolate salivary entry or bile and pancreatic secretion at the duodenum.
gaps: Nine food-segment rims coincide. The accessory overlays meet recipient surfaces. The exterior plate preserves local anatomy, while the separate conduit shows route order.
sources: Workshop shared frame and gastric limits
baselineCombined: Stomach, liver, gallbladder and pancreas exteriors. Duct continuity is outside this plate.
Small and large bowel shown together from their respective native export coordinates. This render illustrates adjacency.

name: Nervous
function: Trace a sensory or motor signal from a peripheral pathway through the spinal cord to the brain.
verdict: Trace a representative right sciatic route into the cord and medulla. Inspect the eye, ear, olfactory neuron and taste receptor, with separate hearing and balance pathways.
gaps: The staged pathway uses authored connections between independent source frames. The selected spinal model contains cord and representative roots. Several roots overlap in the straight view.
baselineCombined: The source cord and representative roots show a regional spinal pathway. Vertebrae are omitted.

name: Endocrine
function: Locate major glands and use the hypothalamus–pituitary relationship to introduce endocrine regulation.
verdict: Locate the glands from head to pelvis. Follow TRH and TSH from the hypothalamus through the anterior pituitary to the thyroid, then inspect the enlarged pancreatic islet.
gaps: The outline and placements provide orientation. The second gonad set sits in an alternative regional inset. The signal arrows and cell cluster are schematic.
baselineCombined: Teaching stalk connects regional landmarks. Its authored surface is illustrative.
Local context from the parathyroid export. The straight view is posterior.

name: Lymphatic and immune
function: Trace lymph from a body region through a node and a collecting duct toward venous return.
verdict: Follow lower-body tissue fluid into a node, a collecting trunk, the thoracic duct and the left venous angle. The thymus and spleen are shown separately from this route.
gaps: Sixteen surface samples and two cisterna containment checks passed. Named bridges connect the capped source duct. The straight node isolate includes a small disconnected source feature.
baselineCombined: Preserved source geometry. The visible line ends are caps.

name: Reproductive
function: Orient both adult tracts and trace one gamete pathway in each.
verdict: Explore the female and male tracts as separate models. Compare fimbrial pickup with tubal entry into the uterus, then trace epididymis, ductus deferens, seminal-vesicle contribution and outlet.
gaps: Both ovary–fimbria gaps are deliberately open. The male ducts and vesicles include authored anatomy. Local adjacency does not establish patent lumens. The breast study remains a separate regional view.
baselineCombined: Uterus, cervix and vagina with same-atlas bladder, rectum and bony landmarks. The ovary study is separate.
Same-source urethral context from the bladder through the prostate and penis. The testis/epididymis study is separate. The outlet context has schematic, unverified lumen connections.

name: Integumentary
function: Show how the skin barrier is built and where surface structures enter it.
verdict: Isolate the skin layers, dermal hair follicle, eccrine coil and its open duct. A separate nail section exposes the plate, bed and matrix.
gaps: Two local teaching scales. The body envelope remains the whole-body locator. The reproduced meshes establish contacts in the illustrated block. Thickness and appendage dimensions are illustrative.
baselineCombined: BodyParts3D male external surface. A continuous exterior silhouette is the evidence available here.
